clue.text: Bang on and vow to support wife or daughter

parts.note: to give your word is to vow, so word means vow
to be for something is to support it

explanation.surface: A cheering instruction: make a promise to back your wife or your daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one continuous instruction, but every short word does a separate job: 'or' even supplies its own letters in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Bang on means exactly accurate, and a word-for-word copy is exact in every detail.

clue.text: Spinning some googly ball, a wily Australian character

indicators.note: Spinning says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Cricket commentary: a crafty Australian spin bowler sends down a googly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' fits the cricket picture of a googly, a deceptive leg-spin delivery, but here it turns the hidden letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The wallaby is a kangaroo-like marsupial found in Australia, hence a typically Australian creature.

clue.text: Celebrity should be about at this time, either side of noon

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
now means at this time

indicators.note: noon starts and ends with the same letter, so either of its sides gives that one letter

explanation.surface: A famous person ought to be out and about around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either side of noon' suggests the letters of noon wrap round something, but both ends are N, so either side supplies just one N.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame, and celebrity in its abstract sense also means being famous.

clue.text: Order collapsed — that hurt transport

parts.note: to fall is to collapse, and fell is its past tense
ow is the cry meaning that hurt
to ship goods is to transport them

explanation.surface: Someone describes a painful accident in which an order of transport fell apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellowship can be a society or brotherhood, the sense in which an order of knights or monks is a body of members.

clue.text: City stroll announced

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken out, so we want one that sounds the same

parts.note: to roam is to wander or stroll

explanation.surface: A city walk has been publicly announced.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy.

clue.text: Bit of cricket leads to some running clashes

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls, one portion of a cricket match
laps are circuits run round a track

explanation.surface: A spell of cricket ends in some arguments as people run about.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is a set of six deliveries from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that overlap occupy the same time, so they clash in a diary.

clue.text: Netted in a flurry with Spain's improved international combination

indicators.note: a flurry is a confused whirl, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A football report: a goal netted in a frantic spell lifted Spain's international side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flurry' mixes up NETTED together with E, the code for Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Detente is an easing of tension between nations, so their relationship has improved.

clue.text: Mark to introduce the Spanish officer

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A notice: someone named Mark will introduce the Spanish officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name but is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer ranking above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: You, for instance, getting deco?

parts.note: a solver who works out that deco hides the word code, rearranged, is breaking a code, as the solver of this puzzle does

explanation.surface: A question asking whether you understand art deco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' means understanding: anyone who sees that deco is just code jumbled up has cracked it, and the solver is addressed as 'You'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who deciphers secret messages is someone who cracks ciphers, as a crossword solver does.

clue.text: Director gets Oscar after broadcast stream

indicators.note: after places the Oscar letter behind the rearranged letters
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A film director wins an Oscar after a streamed broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The film-awards picture is a decoy: 'broadcast' rearranges STREAM, and Oscar is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished conductor, someone who directs an orchestra.

clue.text: On strike, rising up and striking

parts.note: workers on strike are out
standing means rising to one's feet

explanation.surface: Workers on strike rise up, and the strike is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outstanding stands out, so it is conspicuous and impressive.

clue.text: Old man seen around English court, Democrat, is one for the axe

indicators.note: seen around means the father word goes round the English letter

parts.note: old man is slang for father, dad
to court someone is to woo them
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: A father seen with an English court and a Democrat who is about to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court but is the verb, to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadwood is people or things no longer useful, which are first to be cut.

clue.text: Earth maybe from track used in exercise

indicators.note: used in means the track word is placed inside the exercise letters

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise
a lane is a narrow track or road

explanation.surface: Soil taken from a running track and used for an exercise session.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one example of a planet, which the question mark signals.

clue.text: Slash quota of curtain material?

parts.note: lace is a fabric often used for net curtains
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A cut in the allowance of fabric for curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: The words read in reverse order as 'ration of lace'; 'Slash' looks like a cut in supply but is a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceration is a deep cut or gash in the skin, so a slash is one.

clue.text: Shops for lads with uniform for nothing

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter stands in for another

parts.note: lads are boys
O looks like zero, nothing
Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone goes shopping for boys who get school uniform free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with uniform for nothing' sounds like free kit, but it swaps the O in BOYS for a U.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop for something is to go out and purchase it.

clue.text: Opponents criticise items used in chess gambit's ending as bluff

parts.note: East and South are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
to carp is to find fault or criticise
chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of the word gambit's is taken

explanation.surface: Rivals scorn the pieces used in the end of a chess gambit as a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' seems to mean a chess deception, but it is a steep cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluff is a steep cliff or bank, and an escarpment is a long steep slope.

clue.text: Most trustworthy US college breaks off course

indicators.note: breaks means the college name splits the off-course word open

parts.note: to be off course is to be lost
Yale is a famous US university

explanation.surface: An American college team breaks away from the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Loyal means faithful and dependable, so the most loyal are the most faithful.

clue.text: Elvis Expo's dished out portions of 'jelly'?

indicators.note: dished out suggests serving things around, so the letters are distributed into a new order

explanation.surface: At an Elvis exhibition, servings of jelly are handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jelly' is slang for gelignite, an explosive, so the dessert picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite, nicknamed jelly, is a blasting material, so amounts of it are explosive charges.

clue.text: Stockade's security measure ten times stronger in the middle

indicators.text: ten times stronger in the middle
indicators.note: the central Roman numeral is made ten times larger, so fifty becomes five hundred

parts.note: a padlock is a security device

explanation.surface: An enclosure's lock is made ten times stronger in the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter L is the Roman numeral 50; ten times that is 500, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a fenced enclosure, and a paddock is a small fenced field for horses.

clue.text: Unprofitable bank

definitions.meaning: ... times are poor, meagre years with little profit
to bank is to tilt or incline, as an aircraft does

explanation.surface: A financial report on a bank that is not making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' seems to be a lender, but it is the verb for tilting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean years bring scant returns, and an aircraft that banks tilts to one side.

clue.text: Triggering literary work upset one's following

indicators.note: following puts the one's letters after the overturned book
in a down clue, upset means the book word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
one's stands for one has, and I've is I have

explanation.surface: A provocative book upset its readers.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' means turned upside down, so the book is read from the bottom up; 'one's' is the contraction I've, one has.
explanation.definitionFit: Emotive language arouses strong feeling, so it triggers an emotional reaction.

clue.text: Inquire in Hungarian time one should be at funeral

indicators.note: in means the inquire word sits inside the time letters

parts.note: Hungary keeps Central European Time, CET
to ask is to inquire

explanation.surface: Someone asks, in Hungarian time, when one should attend a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A casket is a coffin, which is present at a funeral.

clue.text: Snatching forty winks after getting wind up

indicators.note: after places the snooze word behind the tease word

parts.note: to wind someone up is to tease, to kid them
forty winks is a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: Grabbing a short sleep after getting annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' is British slang for tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapping is seizing a person by force, so snatching is the act.

clue.text: Fare taken aboard from a car on island

indicators.note: taken aboard means the answer is carried inside the following words

explanation.surface: Passengers' food is brought on board a car ferry to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price, but it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a pasta, an example of food, which fare means.

clue.text: Violet Elizabeth's title for fairy story

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott, the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William books, turns her s sounds into th

parts.note: Miss is a title for an unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl from the Just William stories names her favourite fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott, from the Just William children's books, lisps, so she says 'Myth' for Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, often of gods or magic, much like a fairy tale.

clue.text: Natural nursery food preparation — right to replace cold starter

indicators.note: to replace means one letter takes the place of another

parts.note: cookery is the preparing of food

indicators.note: starter here means the opening letter of the word cold is the one taken

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip for preparing natural nursery food: use the right ingredient instead of a cold starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold starter' sounds like a chilled first course but is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookery is a colony where rooks breed and rear chicks, a nursery in nature.

clue.text: Clue to make rum link with gin

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters are shaken into a different order

explanation.surface: Advice for a cocktail: mix rum with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit, but it is the adjective meaning strange, rearranging LINK and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or suggestion, a clue to something.

clue.text: Slim cuisine?

parts.note: cuisine can mean the place where food is cooked, and a slim one is a small one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slim cuisine' suggests diet food, but cuisine is read as the French word for a kitchen and slim as small.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny cooking area, smaller than a full kitchen, is a narrow cooking space.
